edition: 2026 First-Year Post-Code on Wages Empirical Report
title: Salary & FnF Disputes in India: 2026 Data Report
h1: Salary and FnF Disputes After the Code on Wages: First-Year Data
metaTitle: Salary & FnF Disputes in India: 2026 Data Report
metaDescription: Data on unpaid salary and FnF disputes after the Code on Wages: delays, amounts, sectors and how fast employers paid after notice.

sectors.name: Information Technology & Software Services
sectors.primaryCause: Notice period buyout disputes & arbitrary asset return holds
sectors.regulator: State Labour Commissioner / Code on Wages Authority

sectors.name: Startups & High-Growth Tech Enterprises
sectors.primaryCause: Runway cash constraints, unvested ESOP clawbacks & sudden restructuring
sectors.regulator: Ministry of Labour & Employment / NCLT Section 9

sectors.name: BFSI & FinTech Entities
sectors.primaryCause: Incentive bonus clawbacks, audit reconciliations & delayed gratuity
sectors.regulator: State Labour Commissioner / Payment of Gratuity Authority
sectors.statutoryLimit: Wages: 2 days; Gratuity: 30 days under Gratuity Act

sectors.name: Retail, E-Commerce & Supply Chain Logistics
sectors.primaryCause: Fabricated inventory shortage debits & unreturned uniform/device security

sectors.name: Healthcare, Diagnostics & Pharmaceuticals
sectors.primaryCause: Training bond forfeiture demands & clinical handover clearance hold

disputeCauses.cause: Notice Period Buyout & Resignation Timing Conflict
disputeCauses.legalStatus: Employer cannot withhold earned wages for unserved notice unless contractually quantified, and total deductions must not exceed 50% under Section 18(3).

disputeCauses.cause: Arbitrary Asset Return & IT Clearance Delays
disputeCauses.legalStatus: Holding entire FnF for uninspected laptops is unlawful; deductions require itemized appraisal and employee opportunity to respond.
Wages definition under Section 2(y) includes remuneration expressed in terms of money; confirmed target bonuses constitute legally enforceable wages.
Gratuity must be paid within 30 days with mandatory simple interest under Section 7(3A) of the Payment of Gratuity Act; leave encashment is part of terminal dues.

methodology.sampleFrame: Aggregated intake and post-dispatch resolution case registry of LegalRecovery.in across 3,420 employee claims from 1 January 2025 to 31 January 2026.
inclusionCriteria: White-collar and technical employees in private commercial establishments across India
Terminal full and final settlement (FnF) or monthly salary arrears exceeding ₹25,000
Resignation, termination, mutual exit, or layoff formalised in writing
Statutory legal demand notice issued via advocate through speed post or certified digital channels
exclusionCriteria: Government, defence, and civil service employees subject to Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)
Unverified anonymous submissions without pay slips, bank statements, or relieving requests
Ongoing criminal breach of trust investigations prior to formal employment resignation

definitions.preNoticeDelay: Calendar days elapsed between the statutory terminal payout deadline (Day 3 post-resignation/termination) and the date the employee instructed legal counsel.
definitions.postNoticeResolution: Calendar days elapsed between verified delivery of the advocate legal demand notice and full or negotiated settlement credit in the employee's bank account.
definitions.noticeResolutionRate: Percentage of escalated disputes resolved financially without requiring a formal conciliation trial or Labour Court recovery petition.

methodology.dataIntegrity: All claim values, dates, and sector classifications are verified against bank NEFT/RTGS receipts, resignation acceptance emails, and advocate service acknowledgments.
